verses.1:1: In the eighth month of the second year under Darius, the word of the Lord came to Zechariah the son of Berechiah, son of Iddo, the prophet, saying,
verses.1:2: "The Lord was angry with your fathers with great anger.
verses.1:3: And you will say to them, 'Thus says the Lord Almighty: Return to Me, says the Lord of powers, and I will return to you, says the Lord of powers.
verses.1:4: And do not become like your fathers, whom the prophets formerly reproached, saying, "Thus says the Lord Almighty: Turn away from your evil ways and from your evil practices." And they did not listen, and they did not pay attention to listen to Me, says the Lord.
verses.1:5: Your fathers, where are they? And the prophets, will they live forever?
verses.1:6: Yet receive My words and My statutes, all that I command by My Spirit to My servants the prophets, which overtook your fathers. And they answered and said, "Just as the Lord Almighty has resolved to do to us according to our ways and according to our practices, so He did to us."'"
verses.1:7: On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month, which is the month Shebat, in the second year under Darius, the word of the Lord came to Zechariah the son of Berechiah, son of Iddo, the prophet, saying:
verses.1:8: I saw in the night, and look, a man mounted on a red horse, and he was standing among the shady mountains, and behind him were red, ash-gray, dappled, and white horses.
verses.1:9: And I said, "What are these, sir?" And the angel speaking in me said to me, "I will show you what these are."
verses.1:10: And the man standing among the mountains answered and said to me, "These are the ones whom the Lord sent out to travel through the earth."
verses.1:11: And they answered the angel of the Lord standing among the mountains and said, "We have traveled through all the earth, and look, all the earth is inhabited and quiet."
verses.1:12: And the angel of the Lord answered and said, "Lord Almighty, how long will You not have mercy on Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, which You have overlooked this seventieth year?"
verses.1:13: And the Lord Almighty answered the angel speaking in me with good words and comforting words.
verses.1:14: And the angel speaking in me said to me, "Cry out, saying, 'Thus says the Lord Almighty: I have been jealous for Jerusalem and for Zion with great jealousy,
verses.1:15: and with great anger I am angry with the nations that join in attacking, because while I was angry a little, they joined in attacking for evil.
verses.1:16: Therefore thus says the Lord: I will look upon Jerusalem with compassion, and My house will be rebuilt in it, says the Lord Almighty, and a measure will yet be stretched out over Jerusalem.'"
verses.1:17: And the angel speaking in me said to me, "Cry out, saying, 'Thus says the Lord Almighty: Cities will yet overflow with good things, and the Lord will yet have mercy on Zion and will choose Jerusalem.'"
verses.2:1: And I lifted up my eyes and saw, and look, four horns.
verses.2:2: And I said to the angel speaking in me, "What are these, sir?" And he said to me, "These are the horns that scattered Judah and Israel and Jerusalem."
verses.2:3: And the Lord showed me four craftsmen.
verses.2:4: And I said, "What are these coming to do?" And he said, "These are the horns that scattered Judah, and they shattered Israel, and none of them lifted up his head; and these have come out to sharpen them into their hands—the four horns, the nations that lift up a horn against the land of the Lord to scatter it."
verses.2:5: And I lifted up my eyes and saw, and look, a man, and in his hand was a measuring cord.
verses.2:6: And I said to him, "Where are you going?" And he said to me, "To measure Jerusalem, to see how great its width is and how great its length."
verses.2:7: And look, the angel speaking in me was standing there, and another angel was going out to meet him,
verses.2:8: and he said to him, "Run and speak to that young man, saying, 'Jerusalem will be fruitfully inhabited because of the multitude of people and livestock in its midst;
verses.2:9: and I will be to it, says the Lord, a wall of fire all around, and I will be glory in its midst.'"
verses.2:10: "Ah, ah! Flee from the land of the north," says the Lord, "for from the four winds of heaven I will gather you," says the Lord;
verses.2:11: "Escape to Zion, you who dwell in daughter Babylon."
verses.2:12: For thus says the Lord Almighty: "After glory He has sent me to the nations that plundered you, for the one who touches you is like one who touches the pupil of His eye.
verses.2:13: For look, I am bringing My hand upon them, and they will be plunder to those who serve them, and you will know that the Lord Almighty has sent me."
verses.2:14: "Delight and rejoice, daughter of Zion, for look, I am coming and will dwell in your midst," says the Lord.
verses.2:15: And many nations will flee for refuge to the Lord in that day, and they will be a people for Him, and they will dwell in your midst, and you will know that the Lord Almighty has sent me out to you.
verses.2:16: And the Lord will inherit Judah as His portion upon the holy land, and will yet choose Jerusalem.
verses.2:17: Let all flesh stand in awe at the presence of the Lord, for He has risen up from His holy clouds.
verses.3:1: And the Lord showed me Joshua the high priest standing before the angel of the Lord, and the devil was standing at his right hand to oppose him.
verses.3:2: And the Lord said to the devil, "May the Lord rebuke you, devil, and may the Lord who chose Jerusalem rebuke you! Look, is this not like a burning stick snatched from the fire?"
verses.3:3: And Joshua was clothed in filthy garments, and he was standing before the angel.
verses.3:4: And he answered and spoke to those standing before him, saying, "Remove the filthy garments from him." And he said to him, "Look, I have removed your lawless deeds, and clothe him in a full-length robe,
verses.3:5: and place a clean turban upon his head." And they placed a clean turban upon his head, and dressed him in garments. And the angel of the Lord was standing by.
verses.3:6: And the angel of the Lord solemnly testified to Joshua, saying,
verses.3:7: "Thus says the Lord Almighty: You walk in My ways and will keep watch in My ordinances, and you will judge My house; and if you guard My court, then I will give you those who walk about in the midst of these standing here.
verses.3:8: Listen now, Joshua the high priest, you and your companions who sit in front, for they are men who observe wonders; for look, I am bringing My servant Rising.
verses.3:9: For the stone that I set before Joshua—upon the one stone are seven eyes. Look, I am digging a pit, says the Lord Almighty, and I will feel out all the unrighteousness of that land in one day.
verses.3:10: In that day, says the Lord Almighty, each of you will invite his neighbor under a vine and under a fig tree."
verses.4:1: And the angel speaking in me returned and raised me up, just as when a man is awakened from his sleep.
verses.4:2: And he said to me, "What do you see?" And I said, "I have seen, and look, a lampstand entirely of gold, and the lamp-bowl on top of it, and seven lamps on top of it, and seven oil funnels for the lamps that are on top of it,
verses.4:3: and two olive trees above it, one on the right of its lamp-bowl and one on the left."
verses.4:4: And I asked and said to the angel speaking in me, saying, "What are these, sir?"
verses.4:5: And the angel speaking in me answered and said to me, saying, "Do you not know what these are?" And I said, "No, sir."
verses.4:6: And he answered and said to me, saying, "This is the word of the Lord to Zerubbabel, saying, 'Not by great power nor by strength, but rather by My Spirit,' says the Lord Almighty.
verses.4:7: 'Who are you, great mountain before the face of Zerubbabel, to succeed? And I will bring out the stone of the inheritance, equality of grace, its grace.'"
verses.4:8: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying,
verses.4:9: "The hands of Zerubbabel—he laid the foundation of this house, and his hands will complete it, and you will recognize that the Lord Almighty has sent me to you.
verses.4:10: For who has despised small days? And they will rejoice and see the tin stone in the hand of Zerubbabel. These seven are eyes that look over all the earth."
verses.4:11: And I answered and said to him, "What are these two olive trees on the right of the lampstand and on the left?"
verses.4:12: And I asked a second time and said to him, "What are the two branches of the olive trees that are in the hands of the two golden spouts that pour into and supply the golden oil funnels?"
verses.4:13: And he said to me, "Do you not know what these are?" And I said, "No, sir."
verses.4:14: And he said, "These are the two sons of richness; they stand before the Lord of all the earth."
verses.5:1: And I turned again and lifted up my eyes and saw, and look, a flying sickle.
verses.5:2: And he said to me, "What do you see?" And I said, "I see a flying sickle twenty cubits in length and ten cubits in width."
verses.5:3: And he said to me, "This is the curse going out over the face of all the earth; for every thief will be punished from this to death, and every perjurer will be punished from this.
verses.5:4: 'And I will bring it out,' says the Lord Almighty, 'and it will enter into the house of the thief and into the house of the one swearing by My name falsely, and it will lodge in the middle of his house, and it will consume it and its timbers and its stones.'"
verses.5:5: And the angel speaking in me went out and said to me, "Look up with your eyes and see this thing that is going out."
verses.5:6: And I said, "What is it?" And he said, "This is the measure that is going out." And he said, "This is their unrighteousness in all the earth."
verses.5:7: And look, a talent of lead was being lifted up; and look, one woman was sitting in the middle of the measure.
verses.5:8: And he said, "This is lawlessness." And he threw her into the middle of the measure, and he threw the stone of lead into her mouth.
verses.5:9: And I lifted up my eyes and saw, and look, two women going out, and wind was in their wings, and they had the wings of a hoopoe; and they lifted up the measure between the earth and heaven.
verses.5:10: And I said to the angel speaking in me, "Where are they carrying the measure away?"
verses.5:11: And he said to me, "To build a house for it in the land of Babylon and to make preparation, and they will set it there upon its prepared place."
verses.6:1: And I turned again and lifted up my eyes and saw, and look, four chariots going out from between two mountains, and the mountains were mountains of bronze.
verses.6:2: With the first chariot were red horses, and with the second chariot black horses,
verses.6:3: and with the third chariot white horses, and with the fourth chariot dappled, ash-gray horses.
verses.6:4: And I answered and said to the angel speaking in me, "What are these, sir?"
verses.6:5: And the angel speaking in me answered and said, "These are the four winds of heaven; they go out to stand before the Lord of all the earth."
verses.6:6: As for the chariot with which the black horses were, they went out to the land of the north, and the white ones went out behind them, and the dappled ones went out to the land of the south,
verses.6:7: and the ash-gray ones went out and were looking to go and travel through the earth. And He said, "Go and travel through the earth." And they traveled through the earth.
verses.6:8: And they cried out, and He spoke to me, saying, "Here are those going out to the land of the north, and they have put My wrath to rest in the land of the north."
verses.6:9: And the word of the Lord came to me, saying,
verses.6:10: "Take the things from the captivity, from the rulers and from its useful ones and from those who have known it, and you yourself will enter on that day into the house of Josiah son of Zephaniah, who has come from Babylon,
verses.6:11: and you will take silver and gold and make crowns, and you will place them upon the head of Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest,
verses.6:12: and you will say to him, 'Thus says the Lord Almighty: Here is a man; Rising is his name, and from beneath him he will rise up, and he will build the house of the Lord;
verses.6:13: and he himself will receive excellence, and he will sit and rule upon his throne, and the priest will be on his right, and peaceful counsel will be between both of them.'
verses.6:14: Now the crown will be for those who endure, and for its useful ones, and for those who have known it, and for the favor of the son of Zephaniah, and for a psalm in the house of the Lord.
verses.6:15: And those who are far from them will come and build in the house of the Lord, and you will know that the Lord Almighty has sent me to you; and it will happen if you earnestly listen to the voice of the Lord your God."
verses.7:1: And it happened in the fourth year under King Darius that the word of the Lord came to Zechariah, on the fourth day of the ninth month, which is Chislev.
verses.7:2: And Sharezer and Arbeseer the king and his men sent to Bethel to appease the Lord,
verses.7:3: speaking to the priests who were in the house of the Lord Almighty and to the prophets, saying, "The consecration has come here in the fifth month, just as it has already done for many years."
verses.7:4: And the word of the Lord of powers came to me, saying,
verses.7:5: "Speak to all the people of the land and to the priests, saying, 'When you fasted or lamented in the fifth or in the seventh months, and look, for seventy years, have you really fasted a fast for Me?
verses.7:6: And when you eat or drink, is it not you who eat and drink?
verses.7:7: Are these not the words that the Lord spoke by the hands of the former prophets, when Jerusalem was inhabited and prosperous, and her cities all around, and the hill country and the lowland were inhabited?'"
verses.7:8: And the word of the Lord came to Zechariah, saying:
verses.7:9: Thus says the Lord Almighty: "Render righteous judgment, and practice mercy and compassion, each one toward his brother,
verses.7:10: and do not oppress a widow, an orphan, a resident alien, or a poor person, and let each one not bear a grudge for the evil of his brother in your hearts.
verses.7:11: But they refused to pay attention, and they turned a senseless back, and they made their ears heavy so as not to listen,
verses.7:12: and they made their heart disobedient so as not to listen to My law and the words that the Lord Almighty sent by His Spirit by the hands of the former prophets; and great wrath came from the Lord Almighty.
verses.7:13: And it will be that just as He spoke and they did not listen, so they will cry out and I will certainly not listen," says the Lord Almighty.
verses.7:14: "And I will cast them out among all the nations that they did not know, and the land will be desolated behind them, without anyone passing through or returning; and they made a choice land into a desolation."
verses.8:1: And the word of the Lord Almighty came, saying:
verses.8:2: Thus says the Lord Almighty: "I have been jealous for Jerusalem and for Zion with great jealousy, and with great wrath I have been jealous for her."
verses.8:3: Thus says the Lord: "I will return to Zion, and I will dwell in the midst of Jerusalem; and Jerusalem will be called the True City, and the mountain of the Lord Almighty, Holy Mountain."
verses.8:4: Thus says the Lord Almighty: "Old men and old women will yet sit in the squares of Jerusalem, each one holding his staff in his hand because of an abundance of days;
verses.8:5: and the squares of the city will be filled with boys and girls playing in its squares."
verses.8:6: Thus says the Lord Almighty: "If it will be impossible in the sight of the remnant of this people in those days, will it also be impossible in My sight?" says the Lord Almighty.
verses.8:7: Thus says the Lord Almighty: "Look, I am saving My people from the land of the east and from the land of the west,
verses.8:8: and I will bring them in, and I will dwell in the midst of Jerusalem; and they will be a people to Me, and I will be God to them, in truth and in righteousness."
verses.8:9: Thus says the Lord Almighty: "Let your hands be strong, you who hear in these days these words from the mouth of the prophets, from the day the house of the Lord Almighty was founded, and from the time the temple was built.
verses.8:10: For before those days the wage of people will not be of benefit, and the wage of livestock will not exist, and for the one going out and the one coming in there will be no peace from the affliction; and I will send out all people, each one against his neighbor.
verses.8:11: And now, not as in the former days am I dealing with the remnant of this people," says the Lord Almighty,
verses.8:12: "but rather I will show peace: the vine will give its fruit, and the earth will give its produce, and the sky will give its dew, and I will give all these things as an inheritance to the remnant of this people of Mine.
verses.8:13: And it will be that just as you were under a curse among the nations, house of Judah and house of Israel, so I will rescue you, and you will be in blessing; take courage, and be strong in your hands."
verses.8:14: For thus says the Lord Almighty: "Just as I purposed to do harm to you when your fathers provoked Me to anger," says the Lord Almighty, "and I did not relent,
verses.8:15: so I have prepared and purposed in these days to do good to Jerusalem and to the house of Judah; take courage.
verses.8:16: These are the things that you are to do: speak truth, each one to his neighbor; render truth and peaceful judgment in your gates,
verses.8:17: and do not, each one of you, devise evil against his neighbor in your hearts, and do not love a false oath; for all these things I have hated," says the Lord Almighty.
verses.8:18: And the word of the Lord Almighty came to me:
verses.8:19: The Lord Almighty says: "The fourth fast and the fifth fast and the seventh fast and the tenth fast will become for the house of Judah joy and gladness and good festivals, and you will be glad; and love truth and peace."
verses.8:20: Thus says the Lord Almighty: "Many peoples and inhabitants of many cities will yet come,
verses.8:21: and inhabitants of five cities will come together to one city, saying, 'Let us go to entreat the face of the Lord and to seek the face of the Lord Almighty; I too will go.'
verses.8:22: And many peoples and many nations will come to seek the face of the Lord Almighty in Jerusalem and to appease the face of the Lord."
verses.8:23: Thus says the Lord Almighty: "In those days, if ten men from all the languages of the nations take hold, and take hold of the hem of a Jewish man, saying, 'We will go with you, because we have heard that God is with you.'"
verses.9:1: An oracle of the word of the Lord in the land of Sedrach, and of Damascus is His sacrifice, because the Lord watches over people and all the tribes of Israel,
verses.9:2: and in Hamath within its borders; Tyre and Sidon, because they were very wise.
verses.9:3: And Tyre built strongholds for herself, and stored up silver like dust, and gold like mud of the streets.
verses.9:4: And because of this the Lord will inherit them, and He will strike her power into the sea, and she herself will be consumed in fire.
verses.9:5: Ashkelon will see and be afraid, and Gaza also, and she will be in great anguish, and Ekron, because she was put to shame over her transgression; and a king will perish from Gaza, and Ashkelon will certainly not be inhabited.
verses.9:6: And foreigners will dwell in Ashdod, and I will bring down the arrogance of the Philistines,
verses.9:7: and I will remove their blood from their mouth, and their abominations from between their teeth; and these too will be left behind for our God, and they will be like a commander of a thousand in Judah, and Ekron like the Jebusite;
verses.9:8: and I will set up a garrison for My house so that no one passes through or turns back, and one who drives out will never again come upon them, for now I have seen with My eyes.
verses.9:9: Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion! Proclaim, daughter of Jerusalem! Look, your king is coming to you; righteous and saving is He, gentle and mounted on a beast of burden and a young colt.
verses.9:10: And He will destroy chariots from Ephraim and the horse from Jerusalem, and the bow of war will be destroyed; and there will be abundance and peace from the nations; and He will rule over waters as far as the sea, and over rivers to the outlets of the earth.
verses.9:11: And you, by the blood of your covenant, sent forth your prisoners from a pit that has no water.
verses.9:12: You will sit in strongholds, prisoners of the assembly, and for one day of your foreign residence I will repay you double;
verses.9:13: for I have bent you, Judah, as a bow for Myself, I have filled Ephraim, and I will rouse your children, Zion, against the children of the Greeks, and I will handle you like a warrior's sword;
verses.9:14: and the Lord will be over them, and a dart will go forth like lightning; and the Lord Almighty will blow a trumpet and will march in the surge of His threat.
verses.9:15: The Lord Almighty will shield them; and they will consume them, and they will bury them with sling stones, and they will drink them down like wine, and they will fill the bowls like an altar.
verses.9:16: And the Lord their God will save them on that day, His people like sheep, because holy stones roll upon His land.
verses.9:17: For whatever is good of His, and whatever is beautiful of His, is grain for young men and fragrant wine for virgins.
verses.10:1: Ask rain from the Lord in season, early and late; the Lord has made manifestations, and He will give them winter rain, to each one vegetation in the field.
verses.10:2: For those who utter oracles spoke troubles, and the diviners false visions, and they were speaking false dreams; they comforted in vain. Therefore they were dried up like sheep and were afflicted, because there was no healing.
verses.10:3: "Against the shepherds My wrath was provoked, and I will call the lambs to account; and the Lord God Almighty will visit His flock, the house of Judah, and will station them as His stately horse in war.
verses.10:4: And from him He looked, and from him He stationed, and from him a bow in wrath; from him will go forth everyone who drives out, together.
verses.10:5: And they will be like warriors treading mud in the streets in war, and they will draw up for battle, because the Lord is with them; and riders of horses will be put to shame.
verses.10:6: And I will strengthen the house of Judah, and I will save the house of Joseph, and I will settle them, because I have loved them; and they will be as though I had not turned away from them, for I am the Lord their God, and I will listen to them.
verses.10:7: And they will be like warriors of Ephraim, and their heart will rejoice as with wine; and their children will see and be glad, and their heart will rejoice in the Lord.
verses.10:8: I will signal to them and receive them in, because I will redeem them; and they will be multiplied just as they were many.
verses.10:9: And I will sow them among peoples, and those far away will remember Me; they will raise their children and return.
verses.10:10: And I will bring them back from the land of Egypt, and from the Assyrians I will receive them in; and I will bring them into Gilead and into Lebanon, and not even one of them will be left behind.
verses.10:11: And they will pass through a narrow sea, and they will strike waves in the sea, and all the depths of rivers will be dried up; and all the pride of the Assyrians will be taken away, and the scepter of Egypt will be removed.
verses.10:12: And I will strengthen them in the Lord their God, and in His name they will boast," says the Lord.
verses.11:1: Open your doors, Lebanon, and let fire devour your cedars.
verses.11:2: Let the pine tree wail, for the cedar has fallen, because the great ones were greatly devastated; wail, oaks of Bashan, because the dense forest has been torn down.
verses.11:3: A sound of lamenting shepherds, because their greatness has been devastated; a sound of roaring lions, because the pride of the Jordan has been devastated.
verses.11:4: Thus says the Lord Almighty: "Shepherd the sheep of slaughter,
verses.11:5: which those who bought them were slaughtering and felt no remorse, and those who sold them were saying, 'Blessed be the Lord, and we have become rich,' and their shepherds felt nothing for them.
verses.11:6: Therefore I will no longer spare the inhabitants of the land," says the Lord, "and look, I am handing over the people, each one into the hands of his neighbor and into the hands of his king; and they will strike down the land, and I will by no means rescue them from their hand."
verses.11:7: And I will shepherd the sheep of slaughter into Canaan; and I will take for myself two staffs: the one I called Beauty, and the other I called Allotment; and I will shepherd the sheep.
verses.11:8: And I will remove the three shepherds in one month, and my soul will be weighed down against them, for their souls also roared against me.
verses.11:9: And I said, "I will not shepherd you; what is dying, let it die, and what is failing, let it fail, and as for the rest, let each one devour the flesh of his neighbor."
verses.11:10: And they will take my beautiful staff, and I will cast it away to annul my covenant which I made with all the peoples.
verses.11:11: And it will be annulled on that day, and the Canaanites will know the sheep that are guarded for me; for it is the word of the Lord.
verses.11:12: And I will say to them, "If it is good in your sight, give my wages, or refuse." And they weighed out my wages, thirty silver pieces.
verses.11:13: And the Lord said to me, "Drop them into the smelting furnace, and I will examine whether it is genuine, just as it was tested for them." And I took the thirty silver pieces and threw them into the house of the Lord, into the smelting furnace.
verses.11:14: And I cast away the second staff, Allotment, to annul the possession between Judah and Israel.
verses.11:15: And the Lord said to me, "Take for yourself once more the shepherding gear of an inexperienced shepherd.
verses.11:16: For look, I am raising up a shepherd over the land; what is failing he will by no means attend to, and what is scattered he will by no means seek, and what is crushed he will by no means heal, and what is sound he will by no means guide; and he will devour the meat of the choice ones, and he will dislocate their anklebones.
verses.11:17: Ah, those who shepherd vain things and have abandoned the sheep! A sword upon his arms and upon his right eye! His arm will be completely dried up, and his right eye will be completely blinded."
verses.12:1: An oracle of the word of the Lord concerning Israel. The Lord, who stretches out heaven, and lays the foundation of the earth, and forms the spirit of man within him, says:
verses.12:2: "Look, I am making Jerusalem like shaken doorways for all the peoples all around, and in Judea there will be a siege against Jerusalem.
verses.12:3: And it will be on that day that I will make Jerusalem a trampled stone for all the nations; everyone who tramples her will surely mock, and all the nations of the earth will be gathered together against her.
verses.12:4: On that day," says the Lord Almighty, "I will strike every horse with panic and its rider with madness; but upon the house of Judah I will open My eyes, and all the horses of the peoples I will strike with blindness.
verses.12:5: And Judah's commanders of thousands will say in their hearts, 'We will find for ourselves the inhabitants of Jerusalem in the Lord Almighty their God.'
verses.12:6: On that day I will make Judah's commanders of thousands like a brand of fire among wood and like a torch of fire in stubble, and they will devour on the right and on the left all the peoples all around; and Jerusalem will still dwell by herself in Jerusalem.
verses.12:7: And the Lord will save the tents of Judah as from the beginning, so that the boast of the house of David and the exaltations of the inhabitants of Jerusalem may not be magnified over Judah.
verses.12:8: And it will be on that day that the Lord will shield the inhabitants of Jerusalem; and the one who is weak among them on that day will be like David, and the house of David like the house of God, like the angel of the Lord before them.
verses.12:9: And it will be on that day that I will seek to remove all the nations that come against Jerusalem,
verses.12:10: and I will pour out upon the house of David and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem a spirit of grace and compassion; and they will look to Me because they mocked in triumph, and they will mourn with mourning for Him as for a beloved one, and they will grieve with grief as for the firstborn.
verses.12:11: On that day the mourning in Jerusalem will be magnified like the mourning of a pomegranate grove being cut down in a plain,
verses.12:12: and the land will mourn, tribe by tribe: the tribe of the house of David by itself, and their wives by themselves; the tribe of the house of Nathan by itself, and their wives by themselves;
verses.12:13: the tribe of the house of Levi by itself, and their wives by themselves; the tribe of Simeon by itself, and their wives by themselves.
verses.12:14: All the remaining tribes, each tribe by itself, and their wives by themselves."
verses.13:1: On that day every place will be opened for the house of David and for the inhabitants of Jerusalem, for removal and for separation.
verses.13:2: "And it will happen on that day," says the Lord Sabaoth, "that I will utterly destroy the names of the idols from the land, and there will no longer be any remembrance of them; and I will remove the false prophets and the unclean spirit from the land."
verses.13:3: And it will happen, if a man still prophesies, that his father and his mother, who brought him forth, will say to him, "You will not live, because you spoke lies in the name of the Lord." And his father and his mother, who brought him forth, will bind him when he prophesies.
verses.13:4: And it will happen on that day that the prophets will be put to shame, each one because of his vision when he prophesies, and they will put on a hairy hide because they lied.
verses.13:5: And he will say, "I am not a prophet, for I am a man who works the ground, because a man brought me forth from my youth."
verses.13:6: And someone will say to him, "What are these wounds between your hands?" And he will say, "Those with which I was wounded in my beloved house."
verses.13:7: "Sword, awake against My shepherds and against a man who is My fellow citizen," says the Lord Almighty. "Strike the shepherds and pull out the sheep, and I will bring My hand upon the little ones."
verses.13:8: "And it will happen in all the land," says the Lord, "that two parts of it will be utterly destroyed and perish, but the third part will be left behind in it.
verses.13:9: And I will bring the third part through fire, and I will refine them as silver is refined, and I will test them as gold is tested. It will call upon My name, and I will listen to it; and I will say, 'This is My people,' and it will say, 'The Lord is my God.'"
verses.14:1: Look, days of the Lord are coming, and your plunder will be divided within you.
verses.14:2: And I will gather all nations against Jerusalem for war, and the city will be captured, and the houses will be plundered, and the women will be defiled, and half of the city will go out into captivity, but the rest of My people will by no means be utterly destroyed from the city.
verses.14:3: And the Lord will go out and do battle against those nations, like a day of His battle on a day of war.
verses.14:4: And His feet will stand on that day on the Mount of Olives, which is opposite Jerusalem on the east; and the Mount of Olives will be split, half of it toward the east and the sea, an exceedingly great chasm; and half of the mountain will lean toward the north, and half of it toward the south.
verses.14:5: And the valley of My mountains will be blocked up, and the valley of the mountains will be joined as far as Iasod, and it will be blocked up just as it was blocked up in the days of the earthquake, in the days of Uzziah king of Judah. And the Lord my God will come, and all the holy ones with Him.
verses.14:6: And it will happen on that day that there will be no light, and there will be cold and frost.
verses.14:7: It will be for one day, and that day is known to the Lord, neither day nor night; and toward evening there will be light.
verses.14:8: And on that day living water will go out from Jerusalem, half of it into the first sea and half of it into the last sea; both in summer and in spring it will be so.
verses.14:9: And the Lord will be king over all the earth; on that day the Lord will be one, and His name one,
verses.14:10: encircling all the land and the wilderness from Geba to Rimmon south of Jerusalem. But Ramah will remain in place, from the Gate of Benjamin to the place of the First Gate, to the Gate of the Corners, and to the Tower of Hanamel, to the king's wine vats.
verses.14:11: They will dwell in it, and there will no longer be a curse, and Jerusalem will dwell confidently.
verses.14:12: And this will be the calamity with which the Lord will strike all the peoples who marched against Jerusalem: their flesh will melt away while they are standing on their feet, and their eyes will flow out of their sockets, and their tongue will melt away in their mouth.
verses.14:13: And it will happen on that day that there will be a great panic from the Lord upon them; and each one will seize the hand of his neighbor, and his hand will be locked against the hand of his neighbor.
verses.14:14: And Judah will do battle in Jerusalem, and will gather the strength of all the peoples all around: gold and silver and clothing in very great abundance.
verses.14:15: And this will be the calamity of the horses and the mules and the camels and the donkeys and all the livestock that are in those camps, like this calamity.
verses.14:16: And it will happen that as many as are left from all the nations that came against Jerusalem will go up year by year to worship the King, the Lord Almighty, and to celebrate the Feast of Booths.
verses.14:17: And it will happen that as many as do not go up from all the tribes of the earth to Jerusalem to worship the King, the Lord Almighty, these also will be added to those.
verses.14:18: And if the tribe of Egypt does not go up or come, upon these also will be the calamity with which the Lord will strike all the nations that do not go up to celebrate the Feast of Booths.
verses.14:19: This will be the sin of Egypt and the sin of all the nations that do not go up to celebrate the Feast of Booths.
verses.14:20: On that day what is on the bridle of the horse will be holy to the Lord Almighty; and the pots in the house of the Lord will be like bowls before the altar.
verses.14:21: And every pot in Jerusalem and in Judah will be holy to the Lord Almighty; and all who sacrifice will come and take from them and boil in them, and there will no longer be a Canaanite in the house of the Lord Almighty on that day.

notes.1:3: The Greek shifts within this verse from "the Lord Almighty" (Kyrios Pantokrator) to "the Lord of powers" (Kyrios ton dynameon), as in 7:4.
notes.1:6: The Greek reads an imperative ("receive") and adds "by My Spirit" (en pneumati mou), whereas the Hebrew MT has a rhetorical question with no mention of the Spirit. The masculine plural relative pronoun hoi ("which" or "who") can refer either to "My words" (tous logous mou) or to "My servants the prophets." It also reads "answered" (apekrithesan) where the MT has "repented/returned."
notes.1:8: The Greek reads "shady mountains" (oreon ton kataskion) where the Hebrew MT has "myrtle trees in the ravine," and lists four colors of horses rather than three.
notes.1:15: The Greek uses the same verb twice for the nations "that join in attacking" and "joined in attacking" (synepitithemai), whereas the Hebrew MT describes them first as "at ease" and then as "furthering" disaster.
notes.2:4: The Greek diverges sharply from the Hebrew MT here: it reads "shattered" Israel, renders the craftsmen's task as "to sharpen them into their hands" (reflecting alternative readings of Hebrew words for "terrify" and "cast down"), and specifies "the land of the Lord" instead of "the land of Judah."
notes.2:8: The Greek reads "fruitfully" (katakarpos), whereas the Hebrew MT reads "without walls" (as unwalled villages).
notes.2:10: The Greek promises gathering ("from the four winds of heaven I will gather you," synaxo), whereas the Hebrew MT speaks of past scattering ("I have scattered you like the four winds of heaven").
notes.2:12: The abrupt shift from "Thus says the Lord Almighty" to "He has sent me" leaves debated whether the one sent "after glory" is the prophet himself or a divine messenger.
notes.2:17: The Greek reads "stand in awe" (eulabeistho) and "from His holy clouds" (ek nephelon hagion autou), whereas the Hebrew MT has "be silent" and "from His holy dwelling."
notes.3:1: The Greek renders Hebrew hasatan ("the adversary/Satan") as ho diabolos ("the devil," literally "the slanderer/accuser"), and explicitly names "the Lord" as the subject of "showed me."
notes.3:4: Continuing seamlessly into 3:5, the Greek shifts to plural imperatives ("clothe him ... and place") addressed to the attendants, without the first-person interruption ("And I said") present in the Hebrew MT at 3:5.
notes.3:7: Following the Greek text as written (without an initial "if," ean, likely omitted before en in early transmission), the opening clauses are indicative rather than conditional. The Greek also renders the promised gift personally as "those who walk about" (anastrephomenous, attendants) rather than "right of access."
notes.3:8: The Greek renders Hebrew "men of a sign" as "men who observe wonders" (teratoskopoi) and translates Hebrew Tsemach ("Branch/Shoot") as Anatole ("Rising," a word used both of a sprouting shoot and of the rising of the sun).
notes.3:9: The Greek reads "I am digging a pit" (orysso bothron) and "I will feel out" (pselapheso, literally "grope/touch"), diverging from the Hebrew MT's "I will engrave its inscription" and "I will remove."
notes.4:1: Greek "speaking in me" (ho lalon en emoi) literally reflects the Hebrew idiom for speaking with someone; the verb exeren reads "raised/lifted me up" rather than "awakened me."
notes.4:7: The Greek diverges sharply from the Masoretic Text, reading an infinitive "to succeed" (tou katorthosai), a first-person verb "I will bring out" (exoiso), "the stone of the inheritance" (tes kleronomias), and the appositional phrase "equality of grace, its grace" (isoteta charitos charita autes).
notes.4:10: "The tin stone" (ton lithon ton kassiterinon) corresponds to the Hebrew term for a plumb weight; unlike the Masoretic Text, the Greek text omits "of the Lord" after "eyes."
notes.4:14: "Sons of richness" renders Greek huioi tes piotetos (literally "sons of fatness/richness"), referring to the rich oil of the olive tree.
notes.5:1: The Greek reads "a flying sickle" (drepanon petomenon) rather than the Masoretic Text's "flying scroll," reflecting a different reading of the Hebrew consonants.
notes.5:6: "The measure" (to metron) renders the Hebrew ephah measuring container; Greek "their unrighteousness" (he adikia auton) reflects a different textual reading from the Masoretic Text's "their eye/appearance."
notes.5:8: The pronoun "her" (autes) is feminine in Greek, grammatically agreeing with the woman (lawlessness) rather than the neuter noun "measure" (metron), though it mirrors the feminine gender of the Hebrew ephah.
notes.5:9: Greek epopos specifically names a hoopoe, whereas the Masoretic Text reads "stork."
notes.5:11: The Greek specifies "the land of Babylon" (ge Babylonos) rather than the Masoretic Text's "land of Shinar."
notes.6:8: The Greek begins with a plural verb "they cried out" (aneboesan) and reads "My wrath" (ton thymon mou) where the Masoretic Text has "My spirit."
notes.6:10: Instead of transliterating the Masoretic Text's personal names (Heldai, Tobijah, Jedaiah), the Greek translates them as common descriptors ("the rulers," "its useful ones," and "those who have known it," referring back to "the captivity") and uses a singular participle ("who has come from Babylon").
notes.6:12: "Rising" translates Greek Anatole (meaning "rising," "dawn," or "shoot," rendering Hebrew "Branch"), preserving the Greek wordplay with "will rise up" (anatelei) and the literal expression "from beneath him" (hypokatothen autou).
notes.6:13: The Greek omits the Masoretic Text's repeated clause about building the house, reads "receive excellence" (lempsetai areten), and clearly distinguishes two figures by placing "the priest on his right" (ek dexion autou).
notes.6:14: Continuing the pattern of v. 10, the Greek translates the Masoretic Text's personal names as descriptors ("those who endure," "its useful ones," "those who have known it," and "for the favor" rather than "Hen") and reads "for a psalm" (eis psalmon) instead of "for a memorial."
notes.7:2: The Greek names Arbeseer the king (Arbeseer ho basileus) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has the single personal name Regem-melech, and treats "to Bethel" (eis Baithel) as the destination rather than the subject.
notes.7:3: Unlike the Hebrew question about weeping and abstaining in the fifth month, the Greek presents a declarative statement: "The consecration has come here in the fifth month, just as it has already done for many years."
notes.7:4: Here, as in 1:3, the Greek uses "the Lord of powers" (Kyriou ton dynameon) rather than its usual "the Lord Almighty" (Kyrios Pantokrator).
notes.7:12: The Greek reads "disobedient" (apeithe) where the Hebrew has "flint/adamant," and includes the first-person possessive pronoun in "My law" (tou nomou mou).
notes.8:8: The Greek has the first-person singular future verb kataskenoso ("I will dwell," echoing 8:3, though possibly transitive "I will settle [them]") rather than the Hebrew third-person plural ("they will dwell").
notes.8:10: All four verbs in the Greek are future tense ("will not be ... will not exist ... will not be ... I will send out") despite "before those days," whereas the Hebrew uses past tenses; the Greek also reads "from the affliction" rather than "from the foe."
notes.8:12: The Greek reads "but rather I will show peace" (all' e deixo eirenen), differing from the Hebrew "for there will be a sowing of peace."
notes.8:21: The Greek reads "inhabitants of five cities will come together to one city" (pente poleis), whereas the Hebrew reads "the inhabitants of one city will go to another."
notes.9:1: The Greek preserves the distinct place name Sedrach (Hebrew "Hadrach") and reads "of Damascus is His sacrifice" (thysia autou), where the Hebrew has "Damascus is its resting place."
notes.9:6: "The Philistines" renders Greek allophylon (literally "foreigners"), the Septuagint's standard designation for the Philistines, distinct from allogeneis ("foreigners") earlier in the verse.
notes.9:9: Following the Greek text, the verse reads "Proclaim" (kerysse, vs. Hebrew "Shout"), the active participle "saving" (sozon, vs. Hebrew "saved/victorious"), and "a beast of burden and a young colt" (hypozygion kai polon neon). Pronouns for the coming king ("He" here and in v. 10) are capitalized following traditional messianic reading; Greek makes no case distinction.
notes.9:10: The Greek reads third-person "He will destroy" (exolethreusei, vs. Hebrew "I will cut off"), "abundance and peace from the nations" (vs. Hebrew "he will speak peace to the nations"), and "waters as far as the sea, and over rivers to the outlets of the earth" (vs. Hebrew "from sea to sea, and from the River to the ends of the earth").
notes.9:12: The Greek reads "You will sit in strongholds, prisoners of the assembly, and for one day of your foreign residence I will repay you double," differing from the Hebrew "Return to the stronghold, prisoners of hope; even today I declare that I will restore double to you."
notes.10:1: Greek phantasias literally means 'appearances' or 'manifestations' (sky-phenomena or visions), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'storm clouds' or 'lightning flashes.'
notes.10:2: The Septuagint reads exeranthesan ('were dried up') and iasis ('healing'), where the Hebrew text reads 'wandered' and 'shepherd.'
notes.10:4: The Greek renders this verse with two finite verbs ('looked' and 'stationed') and 'a bow in wrath,' diverging from the Hebrew nouns 'cornerstone,' 'tent peg,' and 'battle bow.'
notes.10:10: The Greek reads 'not even one of them will be left behind,' whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'no room will be found for them.'
notes.11:7: The Greek reads the proper name 'into Canaan' (Chanaanitin, and 'the Canaanites' in 11:11) where the Hebrew has 'therefore, the afflicted of [the flock]'; Schoinisma ('Allotment') literally denotes a portion measured out with a cord, corresponding to Hebrew 'Union.'
notes.11:10: The Saints Greek text reads third-person plural lempsontai ('they will take') before first-person aporripso ('I will cast away'), reflecting the broader alternation between future and past tenses in the Septuagint of 11:7-14.
notes.11:11: The Greek uses the LXX-distinct proper name hoi Chananaioi ('the Canaanites') as the subject and takes 'the sheep that are guarded for me' as the object, followed by dioti ('for').
notes.11:13: Greek choneuterion means 'smelting furnace' (where the Hebrew reads 'the potter'), and third-person singular edokimasthe ('it was tested') matches the metal-assaying imagery rather than Hebrew first-person 'I was valued.'
notes.11:14: Greek kataschesin means 'possession' or 'allotted holding,' where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads 'brotherhood.'
notes.12:2: Greek prothyra saleuomena means 'shaken doorways' (reading Hebrew saph as 'threshold/porch' rather than 'cup'), and the Greek specifies 'in Judea there will be a siege.'
notes.12:3: The Septuagint reads 'a trampled stone' and active/middle empaizon empaixetai ('will surely mock'), where the Hebrew reads 'a heavy stone; all who lift it will severely injure themselves.'
notes.12:10: Greek anth' hon katorchesanto literally means 'because they danced in mockery/triumph,' where the Hebrew Masoretic Text (and John 19:37) reads 'whom they pierced.' Capitalizing third-person auton ('for Him') after first-person 'to Me' reflects traditional messianic/divine identification; Greek makes no case distinction.
notes.12:11: The Septuagint renders Hebrew 'Hadad-rimmon in the plain of Megiddo' as 'a pomegranate grove being cut down in a plain.'
notes.12:13: The Greek reads the LXX-distinct proper name Symeon ('Simeon'), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has 'Shimei.'
notes.13:1: The Greek reads "every place" where the Hebrew MT has "a fountain," and "for removal and for separation" corresponding to Hebrew "for sin and for impurity."
notes.13:2: Here alone in Zechariah the Greek transliterates Hebrew sabaoth ('hosts/armies') directly as Κύριος σαβαώθ ('the Lord Sabaoth') rather than translating it as Κύριος Παντοκράτωρ ('the Lord Almighty').
notes.13:3: Greek sympodizo ("bind" or "tie the feet of") differs markedly from the Hebrew MT reading "pierce him through."
notes.13:4: Unlike the Hebrew MT ("they will not wear a hairy cloak in order to deceive"), the Greek lacks the negation and reads positively that they will put on a hairy hide because they lied.
notes.13:5: Greek egennesen ("brought forth / fathered") reflects taking the Hebrew verb qanah ("acquired/bought") in its sense of "produce/beget."
notes.13:7: The Greek reads plural "shepherds" and plural imperatives "Strike ... and pull out" (ekspasate), differing from both the Hebrew MT ("strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered") and the New Testament citation in Matthew 26:31 and Mark 14:27.
notes.14:5: The Greek reads "will be blocked up" (phrachthesetai / enphrachthesetai) where the Hebrew MT has "you will flee," uses the LXX-distinct place name "Iasod" (Hebrew "Azal"), and closes with "with Him" (Hebrew "with you").
notes.14:8: The Greek reads "in spring" (en eari) where the Hebrew MT has "in winter," and renders the eastern and western seas literally as "the first sea" and "the last sea."
notes.14:10: The Greek begins with the participle "encircling" continuing from 14:9, reads the Hebrew verb for "be lifted up" as the place name "Ramah," and reads "Hanamel" (Anameel) where the Hebrew MT has "Hananel."
notes.14:17: Instead of the Hebrew MT's "upon them there will be no rain," the Greek reads "these also will be added to those" (linking them with the afflicted nations) and likewise omits any mention of rain in 14:18.
notes.14:20: The Greek reads "what is on the bridle of the horse" where the Hebrew MT has "the bells of the horses," and treats "holy to the Lord Almighty" as a predicate adjective parallel to 14:21.
